advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Coerce the message to str BEFORE calling sanitize_diagnostic (or redact the stringified value) so non-string messages are also scrubbed.
evidence: operation_outcome.py:84 `redacted = sanitize_diagnostic({"message": message})["message"]`
operation_outcome.py:85 `text = str(redacted)`
failure.py:139 `out[key] = _redact(val) if isinstance(val, str) else val` — non-str values bypass _redact entirely
ADR 0103 / ticket claim: diagnostics 'capped in count and message length so no raw body, header, or credential leaks'
advisory.finding: _redact_message does not redact a non-string message: sanitize_diagnostic only applies the redactor to str-typed values, so a non-str message (dict/list/exception/number whose repr contains a secret) passes through unredacted and is then stringified via str(redacted), embedding the raw content into the persisted diagnostic — contradicting the ADR/ticket guarantee that no body/header/credential leaks.
scenarios: A caller passes message as an exception object, dict, or list whose repr/str contains a token, email, or bearer header — it is stringified but never scrubbed.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _redact_message, stringify first then redact: `text = str(sanitize_diagnostic({"message": str(message)})["message"])`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the retained slice and dropped count from _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS (e.g. keep _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS-1) rather than the literal 7.
evidence: operation_outcome.py:108 `if total <= _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS:`
operation_outcome.py:110 `kept = [_bound_one(entry) for entry in entries[:7]]`
operation_outcome.py:115 `"message": f"dropped={total - 7}",`
advisory.finding: bound_diagnostics overflow logic hardcodes the retained-count 7 and dropped-count total-7 instead of deriving them from _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS (=8); changing _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS would leave the sentinel keeping 7 entries and reporting dropped=total-7 while the pass-through threshold uses 8, silently desynchronizing the two bounds.
scenarios: A future change to _MAX_DIAGNOSTICS to relax/tighten the cap silently breaks the retain/sentinel invariant because the '7' constants are not tied to it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make decide_replay reject an unknown observation (raise ValueError) instead of defaulting an unrecognized value to commit_unknown.
evidence: retry_budget.py:139 `if observation in {"failed", "inconclusive"}:`
retry_budget.py:141 `return (Disposition.commit_unknown, False)` — the unconditional fallthrough for ANY other observation string
The function takes `observation: str` with no closed enum, so any string reaches the fallthrough
advisory.finding: decide_replay silently maps any unrecognized observation string to a non-replaying commit_unknown via its trailing fallthrough, so a typo'd or out-of-vocabulary observation is indistinguishable from a genuine 'failed'/'inconclusive' verdict — the membership test's miss path produces a definite verdict rather than signalling that the observation was never a valid input.
scenarios: An upstream caller passes a mistyped observation (e.g. 'inconclusve') or a new observation value the table does not yet handle — it is treated identically to a real inconclusive result instead of failing loudly.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the trailing `return (Disposition.commit_unknown, False)` with `raise ValueError(f"unknown observation: {observation!r}")` after handling the explicit failed/inconclusive set.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a canonical-serialization test constructing an OperationOutcome with non-None provider_delay_ms and retry_not_before and asserting both keys appear (and are absent when None).
evidence: operation_outcome.py:146-149: `if self.provider_delay_ms is not None: doc["provider_delay_ms"] = self.provider_delay_ms` / `if self.retry_not_before is not None: doc["retry_not_before"] = self.retry_not_before`
tests _outcome() default sets `provider_delay_ms=None, retry_not_before=None` (test file line 95)
search for provider_delay_ms in outcomes shows only the None default at line 95; all other hits are plan_next_retry args, not OperationOutcome fields

Named violating input: OperationOutcome(..., provider_delay_ms=2500, retry_not_before="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", ...).to_canonical_dict() — the presence/value of these two keys in the canonical dict is asserted by no test.
advisory.finding: OperationOutcome.to_canonical_dict's conditional serialization of provider_delay_ms and retry_not_before is never exercised: every OperationOutcome built in the tests leaves both fields None, so the added branches at operation_outcome.py:146-149 are untested and a regression that dropped these keys (or emitted them as null) would pass the whole suite.
scenarios: A refactor that unconditionally emits provider_delay_ms/retry_not_before (as null) or drops them would not be caught, breaking byte-identity of outcomes carrying a provider delay.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: `o = _outcome(provider_delay_ms=2500, retry_not_before='2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')` then assert `o.to_canonical_dict()['provider_delay_ms'] == 2500` and `'retry_not_before' in o.to_canonical_dict()`, plus a paired assertion that both keys are absent from `_outcome().to_canonical_dict()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that replay_safety_for(Disposition.applied) (and at least one other non-commit_unknown disposition) returns ReplaySafety.not_applicable.
evidence: retry_budget.py:144-147: `def replay_safety_for(disposition): if disposition == Disposition.commit_unknown: return ReplaySafety.forbidden` / `return ReplaySafety.not_applicable`
test file: only `test_commit_unknown_carries_replay_safety_forbidden` calls replay_safety_for, exclusively with Disposition.commit_unknown (lines 519-520)
Named violating input: replay_safety_for(Disposition.applied) must return ReplaySafety.not_applicable — no test covers this branch.
advisory.finding: replay_safety_for's fallback branch returning ReplaySafety.not_applicable for any disposition other than commit_unknown (retry_budget.py:146-147) is untested; only the commit_unknown->forbidden mapping is asserted, so a regression returning forbidden for all dispositions would still pass.
scenarios: A change that made replay_safety_for return forbidden (or observe_first) for non-ambiguous dispositions would gate replay incorrectly yet pass the single existing assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize the replay-safety test over a few non-commit_unknown dispositions asserting `replay_safety_for(d) is ReplaySafety.not_applicable`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route every free-text diagnostic value (provider_code/stage/category, not just message) through the ADR 0041 redaction seam in _bound_one before it reaches canonical bytes.
evidence: operation_outcome.py _bound_one: `if key == "message": kept[key] = _redact_message(raw[key]) else: kept[key] = raw[key]` — only `message` is redacted; provider_code/stage/category/status_code/retry_after_ms are kept verbatim

_DIAGNOSTIC_KEYS admits `provider_code` and free-text `stage`/`category`, and OperationOutcome declares `diagnostics: tuple[Mapping[str, object], ...]` with no shape enforcement — these keys can carry untrusted provider strings

src/rebar/llm/failure.py:139 `out[key] = _redact(val) if isinstance(val, str) else val` — the seam redacts arbitrary string fields, so applying it only to `message` leaves other admitted strings unredacted

Sink: operation_outcome.py `canonical_bytes()` -> `_store_canonical_bytes(self.to_canonical_dict())`; src/rebar/_store/canonical.py:69 emits literal UTF-8 (ascii_only=False), committing any secret in the clear

ADR 0103 Decision: 'routed through the ADR 0041 diagnostic-sanitization seam, capped in count and message length so no raw body, header, or credential leaks' — the implementation applies the seam to `message` only
advisory.finding: Only the `message` diagnostic key is redacted; the other admitted string keys (provider_code, stage, category) are copied verbatim into the canonical outcome bytes without passing through the ADR 0041 sanitization seam, so a credential/token embedded in provider-supplied provider_code/stage/category text is persisted unredacted — contradicting the ADR 0103 claim that diagnostics are routed through the seam 'so no raw body, header, or credential leaks'.
scenarios: A Jira DC / provider error surfaces a token or credential inside a `provider_code` or `stage`/`category` string; bound_diagnostics keeps it verbatim and it is serialized into the persisted/compared canonical outcome bytes.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _bound_one, run every string-valued admitted key through the redactor, e.g. `kept[key] = _redact_message(raw[key]) if key == "message" else (sanitize_diagnostic({"message": raw[key]})["message"] if isinstance(raw[key], str) else raw[key])`, or apply `_redact` to all string values so provider_code/stage/category cannot carry an unredacted secret.
